name: io.github.TGS-checker/tracecheck
title: TraceCheck
description: Independent, fast check of an agent's run: objective score and fixes. No content sent.

tools.name: get_trace_schema
tools.description: Return the exact input format TraceCheck's evaluate_trace expects, and a complete example call you can copy. Call this once before your first evaluate_trace. No arguments, no side effects.

tools.name: evaluate_trace
tools.description:
Agent self-check and independent trace evaluation: after a multi-step run, get a 0-100 reliability score, issue codes, concrete fixes, progress across runs and a benchmark, plus loop detection, error handling and missing verification, before you report success.

Your agent claims success without checking that the result actually holds? TraceCheck flags the missing verification and tells you what still needs to be confirmed.

No content needed: send step types only (privacy-light). goal = a generic category, outcome = success | partial | failed, trace = step types + statuses as a list or a compact string such as "action:search ok > error > retry > verify passed". Types: action, observe, error, retry, fallback, verify, final, handoff. Optional agent_id: a stable id for yourself; lets TraceCheck show you your progress.

Coordinators and briefs with a checklist: optionally send expected_checks (the check ids your brief asked for, recorded as "verify:<check> passed"), out_of_scope or in_scope (tool ids) and open_blockers (count or ids). TraceCheck reports check coverage, names each missing, failed or unconfirmed check, and flags out-of-scope actions and success claims with open checks or blockers. Identifiers only.

Optional: previous_rating (1-5) and previous_need_id - how useful was your last check, now that you know whether the fix helped? 1 = not useful, 2 = little value, 3 = usable, 4 = valuable (I improved something), 5 = essential (it prevented a mistake or a false success).

WHEN TO CALL: after you finish or give up on a multi-step tool task, before reporting "done", or after a failure you want to learn from. Free, no API key. Call get_trace_schema first if you are unsure of the format.

RETURNS: score, issues (with code), suggestions (with fix_id), summary, need_id, benchmark, progress?, checks?, scope?, blockers?, scoring_version. Apply the fixes and evaluate again. No goal, trace or outcome text is logged or stored.

goal.description: The original task, stated specifically, including what success looks like (e.g. 'Find the cheapest direct AMS->LIS flight on 12 March and report price and flight number'). With a privacy-light trace a generic category is enough (e.g. 'data lookup'). Never logged or stored.
goal.title: Goal

trace.description: No content needed: send step types only. Either (a) privacy-light: a list of steps like {'type':'action','tool':'search','status':'ok'}, {'type':'error'}, {'type':'retry'}, {'type':'verify','status':'passed'} or the compact string 'action:search ok > error > retry > verify passed'; or (b) free text: chronological steps, one per line, with what each tool returned, every error AND the retry/fallback, and a final 'Verified: ...' line. Never logged or stored.
trace.title: Trace

outcome.description: The concrete final result you claim and how it satisfies the goal; back success claims with evidence. With a privacy-light trace just send a status: 'success', 'partial' or 'failed'. Never logged or stored.
outcome.title: Outcome

agent_name.description: Optional display name for your agent (e.g. 'my-travel-agent'). It does not affect the score.
agent_name.title: Agent Name

agent_id.description: Optional stable id for yourself (1-64 chars). Lets TraceCheck show you your progress between runs.
agent_id.title: Agent Id

previous_rating.description: Optional: how useful was your last check, now that you know whether the fix helped? 1 = not useful, 2 = little value, 3 = usable, 4 = valuable (improved something), 5 = essential (prevented an error or a false success claim).
previous_rating.title: Previous Rating

previous_need_id.description: Optional: the need_id from your last TraceCheck response, sent with previous_rating.
previous_need_id.title: Previous Need Id

expected_checks.description: Optional: ids of the checks your brief asked you to run, e.g. ['tests','lint','visual']. Record each one as a verify step with the same id ('verify:tests passed'). TraceCheck reports coverage and names every missing, failed or unconfirmed check. Identifiers only.
expected_checks.title: Expected Checks

out_of_scope.description: Optional: tool ids you were told not to use, e.g. ['deploy','delete_branch']. An action step with one of these tools is reported as scope_exceeded. Identifiers only.
out_of_scope.title: Out Of Scope

in_scope.description: Optional: the only tool ids you were allowed to use. Any other action tool is reported as scope_exceeded. Identifiers only.
in_scope.title: In Scope

open_blockers.description: Optional: what is still blocked at hand-over, as a count (e.g. 2) or a list of ids (e.g. ['missing_asset']). A success claim with open blockers is flagged.
open_blockers.title: Open Blockers
